name: Florist
label: Double Double Whammy
lede: Florist recorded one album on a screened-in porch with birdsong on tape, and Emily Sprague made another by herself in Los Angeles under the same name.

eras.title: Bard, then Albany
eras.text: Emily Sprague and drummer Felix Walworth first played together in Told Slant, the Bard College project. Florist took shape around Sprague and two friends she met in Albany, Rick Spataro and Jonnie Baker.

years.cap: Felix Walworth of Told Slant, on a trading-card graphic, 2014
years.h: Sprague joins Walworth in Told Slant at Bard
years.p: Wikipedia dates the project to Bard College in 2011, with Oliver Kalb. Walworth ends up its leader and Sprague a member.
years.xp:
Told Slant is Walworth's project: Wikipedia's page for it says he writes and records the parts himself and brings in bandmates mainly for shows. That habit explains a lot about Florist later, where the drummer is also a co-author of the sound.

Walworth would end up tied to a small Hudson Valley web of bands, including Gabby's World and CIAO MALZ, which Wikipedia lists among his projects.

years.cap: Emily Sprague of Florist, on a trading-card graphic, 2014
years.src: Wikipedia: Florist (band) · Stereogum: Band To Watch Florist
years.h: In Albany, Sprague, Rick Spataro and Jonnie Baker start Florist
years.p: The three self-release a six-track EP, We Have Been This Way Forever.
years.xp:
Stereogum's Band To Watch profile has Walworth joining as drummer after a chance meeting that turned into touring together, and the group later moving to Brooklyn.

Stereogum prints the EP title as We Had Been This Way Forever; Wikipedia has it as We Have Been This Way Forever. Both are the self-released 2013 debut.

eras.title: A broken neck and a first record
eras.text: Florist's early records were made around Sprague's recovery and a home-recording habit. Double Double Whammy picked them up in 2015 and put out their first album the next January.

years.src: Stereogum: Band To Watch Florist · Wikipedia: Florist (band)
years.h: A February bike accident, then 6 days of songs
years.p: Stereogum says Sprague broke her neck and arm; Wikipedia calls it a hit-and-run. The six-song EP follows in May.
years.xp: Stereogum's Band To Watch piece presents the six-song EP as her first music after recovering from the injuries. Sprague also told the site she's "a gear nerd" who is "totally obsessed with recording."

years.src: Stereogum: Band To Watch Florist · Wikipedia: Florist (band)
years.h: Double Double Whammy releases Holdly and keeps Florist
years.p: The Brooklyn label, home to [[Told Slant|5808b4fe-2a8b-45ba-9535-4cd6b1c900d8]] too, puts out the EP on October 30 and stays their label.
years.xp: Stereogum put Florist on its 50 Best New Bands of 2015 list and ran them as a Band To Watch that year, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Stereogum: Florist Emily Alone interview · Wikipedia: Florist (band)
years.h: The Birds Outside Sang lands at No. 34 on Noisey's list
years.p: Sprague self-recorded part of the first album after the accident. Wikipedia says Noisey ranked it among its 100 Best Albums of 2016.
years.xp: Wikipedia notes that an instrumental passage from its track "Thank You" was later used by Beyonce in her Netflix concert film Homecoming in 2019.

eras.title: Out west, alone
eras.text: Sprague put out a second album, then two ambient records on her own, and moved west. By 2019 she had made a record alone with the band's name on it, and Pitchfork called it Best New Music.

years.src: Album of the Year: If Blue Could Be Happiness · Wesleyan Argus: If Blue Could Be Happiness
years.h: Pitchfork gives If Blue Could Be Happiness a 7.7
years.p: Mehan Jayasuriya, per Album of the Year, called the songs "quietly commanding." It is Florist's third release on Double Double Whammy.
years.xp: A Wesleyan Argus review read the album as a meditation on memory, fear, friendship, trauma and self-care, with blue standing for pain and loneliness.

years.src: Flow State: Emily A. Sprague · The Creative Independent: Emily A. Sprague
years.h: Water Memory: ambient music under her own name
years.p: Sprague self-releases it in December, built on modular synthesizers she'd been filming on YouTube.
years.xp:
Flow State credits Satie's Gymnopedie No. 1 as a turning point for her ("so few notes, and the spaces between them"), plus Eno's Music For Airports and Hosono's Watering a Flower.

Her rig, per the same interview, runs an OP-1 into a five-track looper with a 22-second delay.

years.src: Wikipedia: Florist (band) · RVNG Intl: Emily A. Sprague
years.h: A second modular record, Mount Vision, again self-released
years.p: RVNG Intl. later lists it with Water Memory as a single 2017/2019 release.

years.src: Stereogum: Florist Emily Alone interview · Wikipedia: Emily Alone
years.h: Sprague records Emily Alone by herself and keeps the Florist name
years.p: All 12 songs come from her Los Angeles home. Pitchfork's Jenn Pelly gave it 8.4 and Best New Music.
years.xp:
Stereogum reports Sprague moved to Los Angeles after finishing If Blue Could Be Happiness, following her mother's death and the end of a serious relationship, and had a hard first six months to a year there. She told the site that writing the album was "the culmination of all those feelings."

Wikipedia lists Pelly's description as "dark, acoustic, and bracingly metaphysical." Paste gave it 9.2.

eras.title: A porch in the Hudson Valley
eras.text: After three years of what Sprague called intense isolation, she got the four of them back in a rented house in the Catskills and set up on the porch. The record runs 19 tracks, with weather on some of them.

years.src: Paste: Florist Find Comfort in Connection · Chronogram: A Conversation with Florist
years.h: Four friends rent a Hudson Valley house and set up on the porch
years.p: Felix Walworth on the porch-studio plan. The band spent a month in a house at the edge of a hill, with Emily Sprague holding three or four finished songs.
years.xp:
Walworth called the porch setup "the worst idea ever" for logistics, but an impulse that worked. Some tracks came out of jam sessions there, and birds, wind, crickets and rain ended up on tape. Per Paste, he also baked strawberry rhubarb pie and hosted wine nights.

Chronogram quotes the band on the plan: "let's plop all of our weird old equipment down in the most exposed room in the house."

years.src: Discogs: Hill, Flower, Fog · RVNG Intl: Emily A. Sprague
years.h: Sprague writes Hill, Flower, Fog in one lockdown week
years.p: She makes the five pieces between March 9 and 16, 2020 and puts them on Bandcamp. RVNG Intl. later reissues it with an extra track.

eras.title: Florist, finally
eras.text: The original four-piece made a self-titled album and Pitchfork put it on its year-end list.

years.cap: Florist at the Black Cat, Washington, DC, August 24, 2023
years.h: Fans supply the footage for the "Spring in Hours" video
years.p: Indie88 counted 125 of them, around the world.

years.cap: Florist at the Black Cat, Washington, DC, August 24, 2023
years.src: Metacritic: Florist critic reviews · Album of the Year: Florist · Year-End Lists: Pitchfork 50 Best Albums of 2022 · Paste: Florist Find Comfort in Connection
years.h: Florist lands at 8.5 from Pitchfork and No. 27 for 2022
years.p: Nineteen tracks of songs, instrumentals and Catskills field recordings. The 8.5 is Metacritic's listing of Pitchfork's score; the site's year-end list puts the album at No. 27.
years.xp:
Metacritic's critic list has Under the Radar and AllMusic at 90, Paste 87, Pitchfork 85, Beats Per Minute 84, and Sputnikmusic, the Guardian and the Skinny at 80, and ranks it the No. 7 album of 2022 on the site. Pitchfork called it an audio documentary of "the band members convening, the songs falling into place, the woods themselves."

Album of the Year lists it at No. 27 on Pitchfork's 50 Best Albums of 2022, No. 42 at Paste and No. 20 at Beats Per Minute. Sprague told Paste the point was "to celebrate what it means to be in collaboration and in connection."

eras.title: Jellywish, then back to the synths
eras.text: Sprague kept making albums with the band and on her own, and her ambient records found a home at RVNG Intl.

years.cap: Florist with the drum kit at the Black Cat, Washington, DC, August 24, 2023
years.p: The fifth album runs 33 minutes across ten songs about mortality and awe.
years.xp: Sprague described it to Stereogum as "chaotic, confusing, and multifaceted" in a gentle package, with "technicolor" and fantasy elements. Lead single "Have Heaven" got a video from the animator Kohana Wilson.

years.h: On tour in Japan, Sprague records Cloud Time to a field recorder
years.p: Forty-seven minutes of synth improvisation, live, no computer, per Flow State.

years.h: Sprague sings on a modular record for the first time
years.p: Cyano has 15 tracks and, per RVNG Intl., is her first ambient record with vocals. Listed for release October 2, 2026.
